resources.string: Lets TVRelay detect when you select a movie or show recommendation on the launcher, so it can open it in the app you\'ve chosen in Settings instead.

TVRelay uses an Accessibility Service to detect when you click a movie or show recommendation on your TV's home screen. When it does, it sends only that title's text to a metadata service (TMDB by default, or TheTVDB - see Settings) to identify it, then shows a "Watch now" button for the app you've chosen in Settings - tapping it (and only tapping it) opens that title there, so an accidental click never jumps you into another app on its own.

Nothing else is read, collected, or sent anywhere. Every other click (apps, menus, anything that isn't a content recommendation) is left completely alone.

You can turn the service off at any time from this app's Settings.

Some recommendation cards - especially the "Top picks for you" row - don't include any readable title in the click TVRelay receives, and voice search bypasses title detection entirely. When this fallback is on, TVRelay uses Android's screen-recording permission to capture what's on screen in those cases and read the title from it using on-device text recognition - nothing is ever uploaded anywhere.

While this fallback is turned on, Android will show a persistent "recording/casting" indicator the whole time, not just while a capture is actually happening - that's a system-level notice you can't hide, and it's there so you always know the permission is active.

You can turn this off at any time from Settings.

If you sideloaded this app and the Accessibility toggle switches itself back off right after you enable it: that's Android's "Restricted settings" protection for apps not installed from an app store, not a bug. Look for "Allow restricted setting" on this app's system App info screen. If you can't find it, connect over ADB and run:

adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.hmartinez94.tvrelay/com.hmartinez94.tvrelay.TvRelayAccessibilityService
adb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1

(The first command replaces the whole list - separate services with a colon if you already use another one, like TalkBack.)

Some recommendation cards don\'t expose their title to accessibility tools, so TVRelay can\'t always detect them automatically. Type the title here instead - everything after that (looking it up, opening your chosen app) works exactly the same way.

Whichever service TVRelay asks to identify a clicked title. TMDB is the default and needs nothing from you - TVRelay includes a shared key so it works right away. You can optionally enter your own free personal API key below instead (get one at themoviedb.org, under Settings → API) - useful mainly if the shared key is ever rate-limited. TheTVDB is available as an alternative if TMDB ever gives you a wrong match for a title.
